## Context

Parent epic `a4bd-4ca8-c44f-49bb`; depends on S1 (`248f-ac00-18db-4259`, closed). S3
(`47a0-7019-da4b-40e0`) makes the inbound removal path decline removals of links carrying no
peer-confirmation record. Without a backfill, the FIRST post-upgrade pass would find an empty
store and decline EVERY legitimate peer deletion — a regression worse than the blind spot being
fixed. The epic states it directly: "Backfill grandfathers existing managed links as
confirmed-at-upgrade (marked as such) so the first post-upgrade run does not decline every
legitimate removal."

This story must land BEFORE S3 turns the decline on.

## Scope

- `peer_confirmations.py` — add `DIRECTION_BACKFILL = "backfill"` beside the existing
  `DIRECTION_OUTBOUND` / `DIRECTION_SNAPSHOT`. `SOURCE_BACKFILL` already exists; the direction
  vocabulary must stay a closed, named set rather than gaining a bare string literal.
- `peer_confirmations.py` — the loader records whether the store file was ABSENT at open (a
  `was_absent` attribute set in `PeerConfirmationStore._load`). Backfill runs on "file was
  absent" (a fresh upgrade), NOT on "store is empty": an operator who legitimately emptied the
  store must not silently have it re-populated.
- `peer_confirmations.py` — add
  `backfill_from_managed_refs(store, local_tickets, binding_store, pass_id) -> int`.
  For each local ticket, read its managed refs via
  `rebar.reducer._managed_refs.managed_ref_set(ticket)` — its kinds are already constrained to
  `MANAGED_REF_KINDS`, so no extra kind filter is needed or wanted. For each `(kind, target)`
  whose `target` resolves to a BOUND peer key via `binding_store.get_jira_key(target)`, write a
  record keyed `(ticket_local_id, target, kind)` with `source_kind=SOURCE_BACKFILL`,
  `direction=DIRECTION_BACKFILL`, `link_id=None`, `confirmed_pass=pass_id`.

**The no-downgrade guard is explicit, because `record()` will not provide it.** S1's landed
`PeerConfirmationStore.record()` overwrites its key UNCONDITIONALLY — it reads the previous
entry only to preserve `first_confirmed_at`. So backfill MUST check first and write ONLY when
`store.get(source, target, kind) is None`. Any existing record (`push` or `snapshot`) is
strictly stronger evidence than a grandfather assumption and must be left untouched. This
read-before-write skip is the entire mechanism behind AC5's no-downgrade half; the upgrade half
needs no new code, since a later `push`/`snapshot` `record()` call overwrites a backfilled entry
by the same unconditional behaviour.

- `reconcile.py::_confirm_peer_links` — **one store instance for the whole evidence step.**
  As landed by S2 this helper calls `open_store(ctx.repo_root)` itself and saves only when it
  wrote records. If backfill opened a SECOND instance, two things break: (a) backfilled records
  would be invisible to snapshot confirmation's fresh disk load, so the same-pass provenance
  upgrade could not happen; and (b) worse, the two instances would race a LOST UPDATE — each
  loaded a pre-write copy, so whichever saves last silently discards the other's records.
  So this story restructures the helper into the single evidence step it should have been:
  open the store ONCE, run `backfill_from_managed_refs` FIRST, then `confirm_from_snapshot` on
  that SAME instance, then `store.save()` once if either wrote. Ordering inside one instance is
  what makes the upgrade work — snapshot's `record()` overwrites the backfilled entry in memory.
  Keep the existing fail-open `try/except Exception` wrapper and the `if persist:` gate exactly
  as they are; no second call site is added to `_persist_and_log`.

- A backfilled record is treated as confirmed by `is_confirmed()`. Distinguishing backfill from
  proof at the DECISION point is deliberately NOT done — that would re-open the blind spot for
  every pre-upgrade link, which is exactly what grandfathering exists to avoid.
- `managed_refs` monotonicity is unchanged; nothing is pruned.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 On a store whose file was absent, every managed ref with a bound target gets a record
      with `source="backfill"` and `direction="backfill"`; the store is then non-empty and
      persisted. Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_backfill.py -k fresh_upgrade`.
- [ ] AC2 A managed ref whose target is UNBOUND gets no record. Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_backfill.py -k unbound`.
- [ ] AC3 Backfill does NOT run when the store file existed but is empty. Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_backfill.py -k existing_empty`.
- [ ] AC4 Backfill does not re-run once the file exists — a second pass adds zero records. Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_backfill.py -k second_pass`.
- [ ] AC5 Provenance never downgrades: backfill SKIPS a key already carrying a `push` or
      `snapshot` record (asserted by inspecting `source` after backfill runs over it), while a
      later snapshot confirmation DOES overwrite a backfilled key's `source` to `"snapshot"`.
      Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_backfill.py -k provenance`.
- [ ] AC6 `is_confirmed()` returns True for a backfilled record. Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_backfill.py -k confirmed`.
- [ ] AC7 In no-write mode (`persist` False) no backfill is written, and a raising backfill does
      not break the pass. Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_backfill.py -k "nowrite or fail_open"`.
- [ ] AC8 The evidence step uses a SINGLE store instance: a record backfilled this pass is
      visible to snapshot confirmation in the SAME pass (its `source` becomes `"snapshot"`), and
      no record written by either half is lost after the single save (lost-update regression).
      Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_backfill.py -k "ordering or lost_update"`.
- [ ] AC9 Every edited module stays under the 800-line cap. Proof: `bash -c 'git archive HEAD |
      tar -xO src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/reconcile.py | wc -l'` per edited file, < 800.
- [ ] AC10 Gates green. Proof: `make lint` exit 0, `make typecheck` exit 0,
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler` exit 0.

## Testing

- New suite `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_backfill.py` covering the
  fresh-upgrade backfill, unbound-target skip, existing-but-empty non-run, one-shot behaviour
  across two passes, both halves of the provenance rule, `is_confirmed` acceptance, the no-write
  and fail-open paths, and the backfill-before-snapshot ordering.
- Regression: `make lint && make typecheck && pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler`.

## Out of scope

The removal decline (S3). No pruning of `managed_refs`. No change to its monotonicity or to
`record()`'s unconditional-overwrite contract.
